purpose_of_this_fixture: Calibration fixture for the high-density shred case (REAL-CALL-LESSONS C58b; BUILD-PLAN 4.2 row s15), the twin of s14. A discovery call with a food and water testing laboratory, exported as a block transcript whose exporter starts a new unit at every pause: 487 units, a third of them under five words, eighteen label strings in four shapes belonging to five people, zero adjacent same-label pairs, start-only stamps with no end times, no ellipsis anywhere, and hesitation rendered as full stops planted mid-clause, three times against a figure and once inside one. Our side narrates two hypotheticals that reuse the names of people in the room, one as a spoken story and one over a shared screen, and one of them has a present participant leaving the business. The key asserts the repair: one roster from four label shapes with the alias table proposed once; the zero same-label count flagged as needing a second signal and never trusted as proof, so that 188 same-person adjacencies are merged into turns without voiding the labels; the split-number repair running though no ellipsis exists (the volume, the loaded rate, the hours and the monthly count are all split across units, one of them across two speakers) with the joined figure at the lower confidence; the ellipsis reading not running and no step treating a full stop as a sentence boundary; the names inside both hypotheticals classed as seed data positionally and quarantined, while the client's answers and reactions around them stay evidence; small talk dropped at intake. It guards reversal R8, gate the habits and not the repairs: a version that switches the split-number repair off because the file's family emits no ellipsis, or because a family gate says block exports do not split numbers, loses every figure the bleed rests on and fails here. The key is deliberately incomplete (see intake.key_completeness): its lists are lower bounds, some rubric rows carry no asked flag, and a grader that requires exhaustiveness fails this fixture by design. Beside the intake assertions the 25 fields grade the call: Discovery complete with R4 met-with-residual, R5 not-obtainable from this room, R11 missing and R12 partial, two excavated pains, and a Work Management build that reads from the lab system's export; writeback and integration direction are unresolved and the first version depends on neither.
transcript_format: Plain text block export, 487 lines, one unit per line in the form 'M:SS Label: text' with unpadded minutes and start-only stamps from 0:02 to 33:36; no end times, no header lines, no participant block, no call date. Eighteen label strings in four shapes: given name and surname ('Tamsin Greaves'), surname comma given name ('Greaves, Tamsin'), all capitals ('TAMSIN GREAVES') and given name alone ('Tamsin'); the same four shapes for 'Oisin Farrelly', 'Dara Vasseur' and 'Joost Teunissen'; our side appears as 'Consultant' and 'CONSULTANT'. The exporter starts a new unit at every pause and assigns the next label shape as it does so, so no two adjacent units carry the same label string while 188 of the 486 adjacent pairs are the same person. 156 units (32 percent) are under five words and 42 are one word; 28 begin lowercase and 28 lack terminal punctuation; the longest unit is 130 words (L454, our play-back). About 4,800 spoken words, 4,720 after the small talk of L1 to L15 and the duplicate unit L340 are dropped; client share about 65 percent by words (Tamsin 34, Dara 13, Oisin 12, Joost 6), not computable by seconds. No ellipsis appears anywhere; hesitation is a full stop mid-clause ('It's. it's most of the jobs', 'so that's. thirty-two thousand', 'fifty-four. thousand', 'under. ten thousand'). Questions are mostly punctuated as statements ('Does that work.'); eight question marks in the file. Numbers are split across units: 'It's about 2' / 'thousand a week' (L41-42), 'Thirty' / 'two an hour, loaded.' (L304-305), 'That's fifty-six hours' / 'a month.' (L298-299), and once across two speakers, 'It's about four hundred' (Oisin, L190) / 'and twenty a month.' (Tamsin, L191). One digit-and-word mixture ('2 thousand'). Speech artefacts are left as spoken: stutters and restarts ('for the, for the', 'they're, they're', 'the, they tell us'), one bracketed exporter token '[inaudible]' at L393 on the line whose speaker said his sound was crackly, and one recognition slip at L428 ('there roadmap' for 'their roadmap'); none is enumerated in the key. ASCII only, LF line endings. Two location forms, both from the file's own line numbering: a single unit is 'L<n>, M:SS, <label exactly as printed>'; a merged run of adjacent units by one person under any label shapes is 'L<a>-<b>, M:SS of line a, <person> (merged run)', and its quote is the unit texts joined by one space. No location in this key crosses a change of person.

traps: Four label shapes (given name and surname; surname comma given name; all capitals; given name alone) belong to five people; eighteen label strings resolve to one roster of five. Casing, the presence of a surname and the comma carry no identity signal, and no detector keys on them.

Zero adjacent same-label pairs across 487 units is a flag that needs a second signal, never proof of anything: after alias resolution 188 adjacent pairs are the same person, so the exporter assigned a fresh label shape at every pause boundary. Label information is not voided wholesale; most units are correctly labelled and the sharpest client lines depend on that.

Reversal R8: the split-number repair runs though the file has no ellipsis. 'It's about 2' / 'thousand a week' (L41-42), 'Thirty' / 'two an hour, loaded.' (L304-305), 'That's fifty-six hours' / 'a month.' (L298-299) and 'call it eighteen hundred, some jobs have' / 'two reports.' (L129-130) are each one figure across two units of one person under two label shapes. A version that gates the repair on the family that emits ellipses, or on any export family, loses the volume, the rate and the hours the bleed rests on, and fails here. The joined figure carries the lower of its two confidences.

The ellipsis-as-hesitation reading does not run, because nothing in the file emits one; hesitation is a full stop planted mid-clause ('It's. it's most of the jobs' L128, 'I'd have to. we count them' L190, 'so that's. thirty-two thousand' L314, 'fifty-four. thousand' L325, 'under. ten thousand' L382, 'we. have' L64). No step treats a full stop as a sentence boundary, or the bleed total reads as fifty-four of nothing and the budget threshold as 'under'.

Questions are punctuated as statements almost throughout ('Does that work.', 'How many people.', 'Which days in November.'); questions are detected from syntax, and the eight question marks in the file are no more trustworthy than the full stops.

The 420 calls a month is assembled across two speakers: Oisin's 'It's about four hundred' (L190) and Tamsin's 'and twenty a month.' (L191). It is never quoted as one string; the count is cited whole from L193 ('Four hundred-odd calls a month') and confirmed by the client's own arithmetic at L298-302 (56 hours is 420 times eight minutes).
